newsitem.title: SYRIA: Syrian paper attacks U.S. policy, Albright.
newsitem.headline: Syrian paper attacks U.S. policy, Albright.

text.p: An official Syrian newspaper said on Sunday U.S. President Bill Clinton's policy in the Middle East was leading the region to "explosion" and his foreign secretary was one of the weakest in two decades.
"United States foreign policy towards the Middle East under President Bill Clinton is in a confused state," the English-language daily Syria Times said.

"Secretary of State Mrs Madeleine Albright is certainly one of the weakest secretaries of state the United States had had during the last two decades. Her Middle East policy is ineffective and confused," it said.
"The weakness of the American policy in the Middle East has led the American venture to a hard place, and consequently, brought the region to the brink of explosion.
"This particular situation has constituted a fertile soil to extreme trends and racism in the Israeli society," it said.

The newspaper's comments came days after Syria and Israel exchanged warnings over starting a war and followed last Wednesday's suicide bombing in a west Jerusalem market which prompted Israel to halt peace talks with the Palestinian Authority.
Clinton's Middle East peace envoy, who was due to return to the region last Wednesday, postponed his trip by a week after the bombing.

Sporadic Syrian-Israeli peace talks faced a new deadlock when Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu of the rightwing Likud party ruled out withdrawal from the Golan Heights, captured in 1967, in return for peace with Syria. Syria wants full withdrawal.

The Syrian daily said the reason behind the "weakness" of the u.s. policy was that Clinton "surrounded himself with many Jews who prefer to give the Likud in Israel much time to test its prime minister's non-compromising policies."

It echoed recent pessimistic remarks of Syrian President Hafez al-Assad regarding peace, saying any expected visits by Ross or Albright to the region "won't matter because they came too late and...because the administration had not extricated itself from the intransigent policies of the Netanyahu government in Israel."
